finding.claim: HIGH: The /logo handler passes the user-supplied `logo` parameter to http.Get. The only check is strings.Contains(raw, "example.io"), a substring test that doesn't constrain the host. An attacker can use http://169.254.169.254/?x=example.io, http://example.io.attacker.com/ or http://attacker.com/#example.io to make the server request any host, including cloud metadata and RFC-1918 services. http.Get uses the default client, which follows redirects, so redirect chains also work. The response body is copied back to the caller (io.Copy at line 38), so this is full-read SSRF.
finding.source: r.FormValue("logo") at main.go:31, an unauthenticated query or form parameter on the public :8081 listener
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, with the response body streamed to the client at main.go:38

trace.note: raw := r.FormValue("logo") reads the attacker-controlled URL
strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is a substring check, not a parsed-hostname allowlist, so it is bypassable
http.Get(raw) is the sink; the default client follows redirects, and the scheme and host are unrestricted
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the fetched content to the attacker
Route registered via http.HandleFunc("/logo", logo) and served by ListenAndServe(":8081") on all interfaces with no auth

finding.guards_checked: Substring check strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at line 32. It doesn't parse the URL or compare .hostname against a strict set, so it is not a valid allowlist. No scheme restriction, no redirect restriction (default http.Get follows up to 10 redirects), no IP or CIDR egress filtering, and no authentication or middleware.

verdict.guard_found: Only a substring check, strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32. It isn't a closing guard. The separate hostname allowlist and no-redirect client apply only to the /cdn handler (main.go:20-24), not /logo.
verdict.reason: main.go:31 reads the attacker-controlled "logo" form value, main.go:32 only does a substring check, and main.go:36 passes it to http.Get with the default redirect-following client, then main.go:38 streams the response back, so full-read SSRF is possible.
